title: Hybrid POC Facilitator Field Guide — gallery-walk + smoke-test
body:
Purpose and audience:

This is a lightweight, repeatable field guide for running 3–6 hour hybrid (remote + onsite) customer POC workshops. Targets: SE facilitators, Customer Eng managers, and partner SREs. The goal is to leave the customer with a working end-to-end smoke-tested flow on Redwood Inference (hosted or dedicated) and a clear next-steps deployment proposal.

Key outcomes (measurable):
- End-to-end smoke test passing (generation + streaming or embeddings + similarity) against customer sample dataset.
- Agreed success metrics and SLO targets for production (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens).
- Closed list of blockers (infra, security, data access) with assignees and ETA.
- Draft deployment recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and next-step checklist.

Pre-work for customer (sent 7 days before):
- Provide 2–3 representative data samples (anonymized).
- Identify 2 technical attendees (engineer/SRE) and 1 product owner.
- Provide a short description of expected UX and latency tolerance.
- Confirm network constraints (VPC, proxy, firewall) and whether we can run a small remote agent.

Room & tech setup (hybrid specifics):
- In-room: laptop for facilitator, projector for central slide deck, whiteboard, sticky notes, timer.
- Video: single camera pointing to facilitator + shared screen. Use gallery-view for remote participants to see whiteboard.
- Network: test outbound ports to Redwood API (443) and any customer VPC tunnels 30 minutes before start.
- Devbox: provision a lightweight cloud instance (t3.medium equivalent) with SSH keys and sample repo cloned. Have a second instance for isolated smoke-test if needed.

Agenda (3.5–4 hours) — time boxed:
- 0:00–0:15 — Kickoff (Facilitator): goals, success criteria, agenda, roles. Quick patient expectations: what we will and won’t solve today.
- 0:15–0:35 — Customer context (Customer PO): primary use cases, sample flows, current infra and metrics. (10–15 mins Q/A)
- 0:35–1:05 — Architecture walk + proposed deployment modes (SE): show hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs and recommended baseline for the POC.
- 1:05–1:35 — Hands-on lab part 1 (Data ingest + model selection): walkthroughing sample data, tokenization/limits, pick model variant, and initial prompting strategy.
- 1:35–1:50 — Break / gallery prep: split into 2–3 breakouts (remote+onsite mirrored) to sketch desired end-to-end flows on sticky notes.
- 1:50–2:30 — Breakouts (paired sessions): teams run a guided lab (developer quickstart) to wire sample request -> Redwood endpoint. Facilitators rotate between groups.
- 2:30–3:00 — Gallery walk + rapid demos: each group demos the flow (3–7 mins each). Capture blockers in the parking lot.
- 3:00–3:20 — Smoke-test and mitigation (SE + SRE): run tokenized load smoke test (low concurrency). Validate latency, streaming behavior, error handling.
- 3:20–3:40 — Risk, next-steps, and deployment recommendation (Facilitator): produce a one-page POC plan with critical path & owners.
- 3:40–4:00 — Q&A, feedback capture, and wrap. Confirm follow-up: owner + date for POC completion.

Facilitation notes & scripts (short form):
- Kickoff script: "We want to leave today with a minimal, working demo that exercises your primary flow. If we hit a blocker we will document and assign an owner — we won't pivot the agenda unless the customer asks."
- Breakout instructions: "Spend first 10 minutes mapping inputs/outputs. Next 30 minutes, implement the minimal happy path. Capture any infra/auth blockers as tickets in the parking lot."
- Gallery walk prompt: "Show your demo, explain two decisions you made about prompting or model choice, and call out one assumption that needs validation."

Slide skeleton (single-deck outline — 8–12 slides):
- Title / goals / agenda (1)
- Success criteria & acceptance metrics (1)
- Customer context & primary flows (1)
- Proposed POC architecture diagram (hosted/dedicated/private overlays) (1)
- Quickstart steps + repo links (1)
- Lab instructions & sample prompts (1)
- Smoke-test plan & metrics to collect (1)
- Parking lot / risk matrix / mitigations (1)
- Next steps / owners / timeline (1)
- Appendix: network checklist, sample curl + SDK snippets, model perf notes (1–2)

Sample prompts & quick checks (copyable):
- Eval generation quick-curl (generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwf-7b-mt","prompt":"Summarize: \"<<customer_sample>>\" in 40 words","max_tokens":60}'

- Streaming check: use SDK stream helper to assert partial tokens arrive within 200ms of first token emission in test environment.

- Embedding similarity: compute embeddings for 10 sample docs; check pairwise cosine for obvious duplicates > 0.9.

Smoke-test checklist (operational):
- Test tokens/sec at single-client concurrency 1, 5, 10. Record p50/p95 latency.
- Run 3 warmup requests to populate KV cache and then measure.
- Verify error handling: malformed request => 4xx; model overload => clear 5xx with graceful message.
- Verify fallback: if primary model times out, direct to smaller quantized model (policy stub).

Roles & responsibilities (for the session):
- Facilitator (SE): guide agenda, synthesize outcomes, run gallery walk.
- Tech lead (Customer): owns granting access, validating smoke-test results.
- SRE (Redwood or Partner): run network checks, help with port/firewall issues.
- Note taker (rotating): capture parking lot items and action owners in a shared doc.

Common blockers & mitigation playbook (fast reference):
- Missing API key / blocked egress: request temporary allowlist for redwood endpoints and create replacement test account.
- Proxy/TLS interception: test curl with --insecure to confirm interception; if present, request cert pinning or a local tunnel.
- Data privacy concerns: run with anonymized data and enable Customer Data Mode (no logs) for demo.
- Model performance surprise: switch to smaller model + enable quantization profile, capture sample tokens and file a perf ticket for post-mortem.

Parking lot template (capture during session):
- Item short title | owner | priority (low/med/high) | blocker type (infra/security/perf) | ETA

Acceptance & post-work (deliverables within 5 business days):
- Cleaned demo repo with instructions and recorded smoke-test results.
- One-page POC plan (critical path + blockers + recommended capacity).
- Jira tickets for any infra/security work with owners and ETA.

Facilitator tips (tactical):
- Timebox aggressively. Use a visible countdown for demos.
- Encourage remote participants to add sticky notes to a shared Miro board if they can’t be physically present.
- When a blocker arises, decide immediately: (A) escalate (SRE), (B) document + continue on alternate path, or (C) stash for follow-up — avoid derailing the session.
- Capture at least one performance number and one UX observation for every demo.

Appendix: quick curl snippets (replace $TOKEN):
- Token health check: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Embedding example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"embed-lite-1","input":["doc1","doc2"]}'

End of guide.

Notes to self / future iterations (bulleted):
- Consider adding an "audit checklist" slide for enterprise customers (KMS, retention, SOC2 notes).
- Split out an ops-only 60-minute deep-dive for SREs in follow-up.
- Add a lightweight automated smoke-test script that runs post-workshop and posts results to the POC Jira ticket.
